next_step: Document post-mortem; follow up Q3 before next promo season; drive product ask for improved auto-burst pricing
notes:
Summary: Marigold Pulse Retail evaluated Redwood Dedicated to replace an aging rule-based chat + search reranker used during heavy promo events. Use-case: omnichannel customer support with live chat and search reranking during flash sales.

Timeline: 
- 2025-10-03: inbound interest from Head of CX; AE Jordan assigned.
- 2025-10-10: discovery call (SE: Priya) 1 key constraints captured: flash sales with 1-3 minute spikes, expected concurrent sessions up to 6k during major promos, need sub-200ms tail latency for interactive chat (perception goal).
- 2025-11-02: POC plan agreed 1 Redwood to validate sustained token throughput and cold-start behavior.
- 2025-12-20: POC run completed 1 steady-state good, but synthetic spike tests showed queueing and tail latency outliers when scaled from zero. Pre-warm reduced but did not eliminate queueing.
- 2026-01-14: Engineering review with infra team 1 asked for guaranteed burst SLA, pre-warm automation, and clear per-promo costing.
- 2026-02-07: Competitor (NimbusCloud) proposed a lower-cost burst SLA with automated managed pre-warm and burst credit model.
- 2026-02-10: Procurement meeting 1 Marigold chose competitor citing price + explicit burst SLA; also noted internal budget hold delayed signing and no exec-level champion to override.

Signals & quotes: 
- "If a promo causes chat sessions to queue, our CS team will refuse the rollout." 1 Head of CX.
- "Your latency looks great at steady state; the risk is the 30-90s promo spikes." 1 Principal Infra Eng.

Technical fit analysis: 
- Workload: high burstiness with very short heavy peaks; sensitivity to queueing and tail latency > primary failure risk.
- Redwood strengths shown: strong median latency, good autoscaling guidance, KV/prefix caching reduced token cost.
- Gap: auto-burst economics and SLA for cold-to-hot scaling; competitor offered lower-cost managed burst credits and stronger marketing around guaranteed concurrency.

Deal outcome: closed-lost to NimbusCloud AI. Primary reasons: competitor price + explicit burst SLA; procurement budget freeze and missing internal sponsor to accelerate commitment.

Post-mortem actions: 
- Capture POC logs and tail latency traces (INF-4973) for engineering review.
- Product ask: consider an auto-burst pricing SKU or burst credits pilot aimed at flash-sale retailers.
- Re-engage timeline: target Q3 re-open (pre-next promo planning).
